Looking at this logical reasoning problem, I need to identify which option does NOT logically agree with the original statement.

**Original:** "Reasonable people will not resist the law violently, unless the consequences of resisting the law are no worse than obeying the law, thus desperate."

Logical form: **If desperately violently resist → consequences of resistance are no worse than obedience.**

Contrapositive: **If consequences of resistance are worse than obedience → will NOT desperately violently resist.**

**Option A:** "Only if no worse, will desperately resist" → desperately resist → no worse. ✅ Agrees.
**Option B:** "If worse, will not desperately resist" → worse → not desperately resist. ✅ (Contrapositive) Agrees.
**Option C:** "If obeying is better, will not desperately resist" → obeying better (= resistance worse) → not desperately resist. ✅ (Contrapositive) Agrees.
**Option D:** "Only when consequences are worse, will not desperately resist" → not desperately resist → worse. ❌ This is the **converse**, not the contrapositive. It reverses the logic.

The answer is **D**.

Options A, B, and C all represent logically equivalent forms of the original statement (direct or contrapositive). Option D reverses the logical direction — it reads as "Only when consequences are worse → rational people won't desperately resist," which is the **converse** of the original, not a logically equivalent form.
